lots.key_photo_findings: The Fortieth: title page reads 'F.C. Green, with a foreword by Sir John Monash, Hobart, John Vail, Government Printer, 1922'; frontispiece is Lt Col J.E.C. Lord with a printed facsimile signature 'J.E.C. Lord' (not a hand signature); pencil ownership inscription 'L.B. Hampson?, Launceston' on the title. Story of the Twelfth: title page 'J. Walch & Sons, Hobart, 1925' so it is the original, not the reprint; three commanding officers portrait frontispiece; jacket or cloth rubbed and soiled. Warburton: green cloth with gilt camels and 'Across Australia', matching the 1875 publisher's binding; half-title 'Journey Across the Western Interior of Australia' with inscription 'From my dear sister Ella, May 1898'. Title page, plates and folding map not photographed.
lots.condition: All three used and worn. Fortieth: white cover titling worn, red cloth marked. Twelfth: rubbed, soiled covers. Warburton: cloth fairly bright, corners bumped, tail worn; completeness unknown.
lots.question_for_armitage: For the Warburton: is the title page dated London 1875, and are the portrait frontispiece, 8 plates and the large folding map at the back all present and intact? For The Fortieth: are all 12 folding maps present? Any loose leaves or foxing in any of the three?
